name: Question 19
problem: Which of the following represents the streamlines of the vector field $F(x,y)=2y\,i+2x\,j$ over the domain $D={R}^{2}.$
worked_solution:
The streamlines of a vector field are the level curves of its stream function and are tangential to the vector field at every point. 

If $F$ represents the velocity field of a fluid flow, then they show the path traced out by a massless particle as it moves with the flow.

A vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ with a simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2}$ has a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ if and only if

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.
$$

Note that 

$$
F(x,y)=2y\,i+2x\,j
$$

 is a vector field with simply connected domain $D,$ where $P(x,y)=0$ and $Q(x,y)=0.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=0,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $F$ has a stream function, since

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.
$$

Next, we find a stream function. A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if 

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\frac{∂ψ}{∂y}=2y,\,\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}=-2x.
$$

Integrating these equations, we obtain the following:

$$
ψ(x,y)={y}^{2}+f(x),\,ψ(x,y)=-{x}^{2}+g(y)
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting $f(x)=-{x}^{2}$ or $g(y)={y}^{2},$ we have

$$
ψ(x,y)={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}.
$$

Finally, we find the level curves of the stream function $ψ(x,y)={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}$ given by the equations $ψ(x,y)=c.$

Notice that the range of $ψ(x,y)$ is $(-\infty ,\infty ).$ So, we will consider level curves for any value of $c.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}ψ(x,y) & =c \\ {y}^{2}-{x}^{2} & =c\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives us a family of hyperbolas with asymptotes $y=x$ and $x=-x$ and, for $c=0,$ the lines $y=x$ and $y=-x.$ Therefore, the correct graph (along with the vector field $F$) is as follows:

EXPLANATION

The streamlines of a vector field are the level curves of its stream function and are tangential to the vector field at every point.

If F represents the velocity field of a fluid flow, then they show the path traced out by a massless particle as it moves with the flow.

A vector field F=Pi+Qj with a simply connected domain D⊆R2 has a stream function ψ(x,y) if and only if ∂P∂x+∂Q∂y=0.

Note that F(x,y)=2yi+2xj is a vector field with simply connected domain D, where P(x,y)=0 and Q(x,y)=0. Computing the partial derivatives, we have

∂P∂x=0,∂Q∂y=0.

Hence, F has a stream function, since

∂P∂x+∂Q∂y=0.

Next, we find a stream function. A function ψ(x,y) is a stream function of the vector field F=Pi+Qj if

P=∂ψ∂y,Q=−∂ψ∂x.

In our case, we have ∂ψ∂y=2y,∂ψ∂x=−2x.

Integrating these equations, we obtain the following:

ψ(x,y)=y2+f(x),ψ(x,y)=−x2+g(y)

where f and g are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting f(x)=−x2 or g(y)=y2, we have

ψ(x,y)=y2−x2.

Finally, we find the level curves of the stream function ψ(x,y)=y2−x2 given by the equations ψ(x,y)=c.

Notice that the range of ψ(x,y) is (−∞,∞). So, we will consider level curves for any value of c. So, we have:

ψ(x,y)=cy2−x2=c

The equation above gives us a family of hyperbolas with asymptotes y=x and x=−x and, for c=0, the lines y=x and y=−x. Therefore, the correct graph (along with the vector field F) is as follows:
